rl.intro1.text: Dabble found a moon-flower seed. It only grows in the Moon garden!

rl.intro2.text: So Dabble is building rockets. Lots of rockets.

rl.intro3.text: A rocket needs a push up that beats the pull down.

rl.intro4.text: Help Dabble pick engines and launch the seed!

rl.between2.text: Liftoff! Rumble had to hold his hat.

rl.between4.text: Now Dabble wants to carry more cargo.

rl.between6.text: Next stop: launching from the Moon itself!

rl.outro1.text: The moon-flower seed landed in the Moon garden!

rl.outro2.text: You compared the push up with the pull down every time.

rl.ready.text: What do you think will happen? Let's test it!

rl.back.text: Welcome back to the Rocket Lab! Ready to test?

rl.prompt.tutorial.text: Drag the engine onto the rocket. Will it lift off?

rl.prompt.engine.text: Pick an engine that can lift this rocket.

rl.prompt.cargo.text: How many crates can we add and still lift off?

rl.prompt.weight.text: This rocket has a mass of {m} kilograms. What does it weigh on Earth?

rl.prompt.engineKg.text: This rocket has a mass of {m} kilograms. Pick an engine to lift it.

rl.prompt.moon.text: We're on the Moon now. What's the rocket's mass here?

rl.prompt.moonEngine.text: We're on the Moon. Pick the smallest engine that can lift this rocket.

rl.prompt.rank.text: Which rocket speeds up fastest? Put them in order.

rl.prompt.fuelNet.text: Some fuel has burned away. What is the net force now?

rl.prompt.fuel.text: The fuel is burning. What happens to the speed-up?

rl.prompt.load.text: Dabble adds more cargo. What happens to the speed-up?

rl.prompt.throttle.text: Fuel burns, and Dabble turns the engine down. What happens to the speed-up?

rl.prompt.mission.text: Reach the target height without going over budget.

rl.help.start.text: The engine pushes up. Gravity pulls down. The bigger one wins.

rl.help.balanced.text: Equal pushes cancel out. The rocket stays still.

rl.help.mass.text: Mass is how much stuff. Weight is how hard gravity pulls on it.

rl.help.moon.text: The Moon pulls more gently, so the same rocket weighs less there. Its mass stays the same.

rl.help.net.text: Take the pull from the push. What's left speeds the rocket up.

rl.help.fuel.text: Burning fuel makes the rocket lighter, so the same push speeds it up more.

rl.help.load.text: More cargo means more pull down, and more stuff to speed up.

rl.help.throttle.text: Work out the leftover push for each kilogram, before and after.

rl.help.plan.text: First find the rockets that reach the target. Then pick the one that fits the budget.

rl.hint.model.text: Let's put the arrows side by side. The longer one wins.

rl.hint.modelTap.text: The glowing one works. Choose it, then press the big button.

rl.hint.more.text: It lifted off! But could it carry one more crate?

rl.hint.smaller.text: It lifted off, but that engine is far bigger than it needs to be.

rl.hint.budget.text: That one flies high, but it costs more than our budget.

rl.hint.short.text: Not high enough yet. More push or more fuel goes higher.

rl.coach.predict.text: Engine on! Now predict: will it lift off?

rl.coach.launch.text: Now press Launch to test your prediction!

rl.idle.text: Build the rocket, make a prediction, then test it with the big button.

rl.praise.1.text: You compared the push and the pull!

rl.praise.2.text: Balanced forces, no liftoff. Great noticing.

rl.praise.3.text: Same mass, less weight on the Moon. Exactly.

rl.praise.4.text: You worked out the leftover push.

rl.praise.engine.text: That engine beats the pull down. Liftoff!

rl.praise.cargo.text: You loaded right up to the limit and kept the push bigger.

rl.praise.weight.text: Mass times gravity. You worked out the weight!

rl.praise.rank.text: You compared the leftover push for every kilogram.

rl.praise.slower.text: More mass, same push, smaller speed-up. You reasoned it out.

rl.praise.same.text: Less push, less mass, same speed-up. Careful thinking!

rl.praise.plan.text: On target and on budget. Careful planning!
